member.summary: Publishes integration events to the message bus after successful persistence. This interface is invoked only by the Unit of Work as part of the atomic commit sequence. Application handlers MUST NOT call this interface directly; they raise domain events on aggregates.

member.name: T:PlantSafety.Application.Alerts.AlertsModule
member.summary: Module marker, constants, and onboarding documentation for the Alerts bounded context.

remarks.para: Purpose: Owns the full lifecycle of real-time manufacturing safety alerts — life-safety emergencies, injury/man-down events, operational & hazard conditions, environmental exceedances, facility/traffic hazards, PPE/behavioral violations, permit-to-work (PTW) breaches, maintenance/equipment health warnings, security/access incidents, quality/process deviations, and compliance/audit lapses — grounded in docs/reference/PlantSafety_Program_Structure_extract.txt, "Comprehensive Manufacturing Safety Alerts" and "11. Alerts & Emergency Response Dashboard".

Responsibilities: Trigger, acknowledge, dispatch, escalate, resolve, and close alerts; classify alerts by catalog category and severity; record multi-channel delivery attempts (PA speaker, strobe, digital signage, SMS, mobile push, wearable vibration, email, SCADA/HMI pop-up, Rave Mobile Safety, PlantSafety dashboard); record response actions and close-out verification for compliance logging & reporting.
Dependencies: None on other bounded-context internals (Maximalist Module Design, Part IV). May be referenced by other modules only through published integration events, never through direct calls.
Inputs: Sensor/IoT telemetry, computer-vision detections, wearable device signals, panic-button activations, human-reported observations, and SCADA/PLC system triggers.

Outputs: Alert read models for the Alerts & Emergency Response Dashboard (Alert Type Distribution, Critical Alerts Timeline, Alert Location Heatmap, Response Time Trend, Multi-Channel Delivery Status, Man-Down Alerts Trend, Fire/Smoke Detection Graph, Gas Leak Sensor Trend); delivery dispatch requests for downstream notification infrastructure.
Events emitted: Alerts.AlertTriggered, Alerts.AlertAcknowledged, Alerts.AlertDispatched, Alerts.AlertEscalated, Alerts.AlertResolved, Alerts.AlertClosed, Alerts.AlertDeliveryRecorded.

Events consumed: None directly (Alerts is upstream/source-of-truth for alert state). Sensor/observability telemetry arrives via inbound adapters in the Infrastructure layer, not via cross-module integration events, to avoid coupling to another module's internal event shapes.

Integration points: Dashboards module (Alerts & Emergency Response Dashboard, Full Program Master Dashboard); downstream notification/dispatch infrastructure (PA, SMS, push, SCADA/HMI, Rave Mobile Safety) via the Infrastructure layer (not generated in this Domain+Application-only pass).

member.summary: Optimistic-concurrency token (native RowVersion projected as a hex string). Populated by the by-id read path (usp_PredictiveAnalytics_GetById); null for list results from usp_PredictiveAnalytics_List. Callers must echo this value back on a subsequent mutating command's ETag field; a stale/mismatched value results in a concurrency-conflict error. Added 2026-08-02 for the Phase 4 full build-out -- additive, does not affect existing GetPredictiveAnalyticsQuery/GetPredictiveAnalyticsQueryHandler callers.

member.name: T:PlantSafety.Application.Dashboards.DashboardsModule
member.summary: Module marker, constants, and onboarding documentation for the Dashboards bounded context.

remarks.para: Purpose: Owns the visual and data-aggregation layer of the platform — role-based dashboard pages composed of reusable widgets (charts, graphs, gauges, tables, heatmaps, maps, timelines, trend graphs, KPI cards) that surface read models exposed by every other domain module. Grounded in docs/reference/PlantSafety_Program_Structure_extract.txt, "Dashboard Design Architecture", "FULL PROGRAM DASHBOARD LIST" (19 named dashboards), and "Appendix E — Dashboard Widget Library".

Responsibilities: Define and version dashboard layouts (name, description, category, primary role, default filters, widget placements); define and version reusable widget configurations (type, data source, refresh interval, parameters, permitted roles); enforce role-based dashboard/widget visibility; model (but not render) the widget data contract (Series[]/Categories[]/Metrics[]) other modules populate.

Dependencies: None on other bounded-context internals (Maximalist Module Design, Part IV). Widgets reference source modules only by canonical module name + query/endpoint identifier (WidgetDataSource), never by direct type reference.

Inputs: Read-model query results and endpoint data produced by every other domain module (Alerts, Risk Management, PPE, Machine Safety, Permits, Scheduling, Observability, Culture, Scorecards, Training, Contractors, Checklists, Security, Environmental, Quality), per "1. Data Sources (Domain Modules)".

Outputs: Resolved dashboard layouts and per-widget data contracts for the Presentation/UI layer, served via GET /dashboard/{id}/widgets and GET /widget/{id}/data-shaped queries (per "Dashboard API Queries").

Events emitted: Dashboards.DashboardCreated, Dashboards.DashboardPublished, Dashboards.DashboardArchived, Dashboards.DashboardWidgetAdded, Dashboards.DashboardWidgetRemoved, Dashboards.WidgetCreated, Dashboards.WidgetActivated, Dashboards.WidgetConfigured, Dashboards.WidgetDeprecated.

Events consumed: None directly. Widget data is resolved synchronously through read-model queries against each source module at render time, not through cross-module integration events, to keep dashboards eventually-fresh without coupling to another module's internal event shapes.

Integration points: Every other domain module (as a widget data source); Alerts module (Alerts & Emergency Response Dashboard, real-time push widgets); UI/API layer (dashboard/widget resolution endpoints, not generated in this Domain+Application-only pass).

member.name: T:PlantSafety.Application.Operational.PredictiveMaintenance.Models.PredictiveMaintenanceRecommendationDto
member.summary: A single recommended corrective action for a PredictiveMaintenanceAlert. Deliberately modeled 1:1 with the alert (RecommendationId == PredictiveMaintenanceAlertId) rather than introducing a new persisted sub-aggregate: there is exactly one canonical recommendation per alert today, templated from the alert's failure type and risk bucket. This keeps recommendation-detail lookup a direct, honest read of the same alert record instead of inventing storage for data that does not otherwise exist. See docs/Phase5/ui-gaps-scoping.md §4.

member.summary: A single sensor-channel time-series point. Values are deterministically synthesized from the alert's real EquipmentId/PredictedAtUtc (seeded, not random) using the real Observability.Telemetry value-object shapes (CycleTimeReading/ProductionCountReading), because no telemetry ingestion pipeline is persisted yet -- see docs/Phase5/ui-gaps-scoping.md §4 risk note. member.name: M:PlantSafety.Application.Operations.SchemaGuard.Services.SchemaDriftEvaluator.Evaluate(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{PlantSafety.Application.Operations.SchemaGuard.Models.SchemaMigrationRecordDto})
member.summary: Evaluates drift for one database. A script counts as "applied" only if it appears as a Success = 1 row; a failed or missing row both count as drift.
member.param: The FULL manifest (all scripts across every phase folder). Filtered internally to scripts whose file name contains (case-insensitive) — the same per-database naming convention already used throughout Migrations\ (e.g. "20-CoreDB-rowversion.sql", "61-archivedb-procedures.sql", both backfilled under their matching database in 70-schema-migrations-tracking.sql). Shared/global scripts that don't embed a database name (e.g. cross-database governance scripts) are intentionally excluded from per-database drift, since they can't be confidently attributed to a single database from the file name alone — a known limitation, not a bug: false negatives on those scripts are possible, false positives are not.

member.name: T:PlantSafety.Application.PermitToWork.PermitToWorkModule
member.summary: Module marker, constants, and canonical documentation for the PermitToWork bounded context.

remarks.para: Purpose: Governs all high-risk maintenance, repair, and operational activities: hazardous tasks must be planned, authorized, controlled, and monitored before work begins.

Responsibilities: Permit template management per category (Hot Work, Confined Space, Electrical/Isolation, Working at Height, Excavation); requester/issuer/closure workflow; scheduling integration; expiration tracking.
Dependencies: PlantSafety.Domain.PermitToWork.*; PlantSafety.SharedKernel. No Infrastructure/EF/SQL dependencies.
Inputs: Hazard assessments and required controls; LOTO/PPE/Confined Space/Hot Work/Electrical Safety module data; scheduling windows from Scheduling.
Outputs: Active/closed permit records; permit compliance scorecards; audit-ready permit documentation.
Events emitted: PermitTemplateCreated; PermitWorkflowCreated; PermitSchedulingCreated; PermitExpirationCreated (see each sub-namespace Events folder).
Events consumed: Real-time PPE compliance and unauthorized-entry detections from Observability used to validate permit conditions.
Integration points: SafetyProcedures (LOTO), PPE, MachineSafety, ContractorSafety, Scheduling, Observability, Auditing.

member.summary: Backtracking constraint-satisfaction strategy: depth-first search over candidate task placements, backtracking on dead ends, bounded by a deterministic node-visit budget.

member.summary: Creates the strategy with the platform-default rule engine components.
Creates the strategy with explicit rule engine collaborators (for testing/composition).

Attempts to place task of , recursing to the next task on success. If no candidate window is feasible, the task is simply skipped (left unscheduled) and the search proceeds -- this strategy does not require every task be placed, only that every placement it does make is constraint-clean.

member.name: T:PlantSafety.Application.Scheduling.Rollup.Models.ConstraintDto
member.summary: Single scheduling constraint row for a job. New-build scope, deliberately kept structural and grounded in real WorkOrder fields only (Assignment/Schedule/Machine/Safety) rather than reusing the Scheduling.PredictiveScheduling ConstraintEvaluator/IConstraintRule engine, which requires SchedulableTask/ResourceAvailabilityWindow/ScheduleAssignment inputs this rollup layer does not populate from real persisted data. Flagged for a follow-up epic if genuine constraint-rule evaluation is required. Only produced for WorkOrder-sourced jobs; empty for PMScheduling-sourced jobs (no constraint data exists on a PMScheduling record).

member.name: T:PlantSafety.Application.Scheduling.Rollup.Models.PredictiveInsightsDto
member.summary: Predictive scheduling model output for a single job. Reuse point: for WorkOrder-sourced jobs, delegates to Operational.WorkOrders' GetWorkOrderPredictiveInsightsQuery (itself a reuse of Operational.PredictiveMaintenance); for PMScheduling-sourced jobs, invokes the same Operational.PredictiveMaintenance alert repository/calculator directly against the PMScheduling record's EquipmentId.
